clue.text: It's a fixed sort of charge

definitions.text: It's a fixed sort of charge

parts.words: It's a fixed sort of charge
parts.note: soldiers ordered to fix the blade to the rifle muzzle then charge with it, so the charge is fixed in a literal sense

explanation.surface: Something described as a set or flat-rate fee, like a fixed price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fixed charge' sounds like billing; the picture is an infantry charge with blades fixed to rifles.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic definition: the weapon soldiers fix to their rifles before charging the enemy.

clue.text: Complain about a rule, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is speech, so the phrase before it is said out loud to give the entry

parts.note: a reign is a period of rule by a monarch

explanation.surface: Someone grumbling about a regulation they have only heard about.
explanation.definitionFit: To arraign is to formally accuse, i.e. lodge a complaint about someone in court.

clue.text: Refuse to be seen away with a student

parts.note: off means away, as in 'he's off today'
L is a learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A student declines to be seen going away with someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' reads as a verb but is the noun: waste, pronounced REF-use.
explanation.definitionFit: Offal is waste parts of a slaughtered animal, hence refuse or rubbish.

clue.text: Give authority to mounted soldiers to secure prisoner

indicators.note: securing something holds it fast within, so the soldiers enclose the prisoner
in a down clue mounted means raised up, so the soldiers' letters are read upwards

parts.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British army corps
POW is a prisoner of war

explanation.surface: Cavalry are given the power to hold a captive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mounted' looks like cavalry, but in a down clue it turns REME upwards to EMER, which then holds POW.
explanation.definitionFit: To empower someone is to grant them authority or power to act.

clue.text: Values seem set for a change

indicators.note: changing the order of the letters of seem set produces a new word

explanation.surface: Someone's principles are fixed in appearance but due to alter.
explanation.definitionFit: To esteem something is to value it highly; both are verbs in the third person.

clue.text: Pound is hit by industrial action

definitions.meaning: to pound is to beat or ... repeatedly
to hit is to deliver a blow
a walkout by workers withdrawing their labour

explanation.surface: The pound sterling suffers because of a walkout.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions in a row, joined by 'is' and 'by'; 'Pound' is the currency in the surface but a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers beating, a single blow and a workers' walkout, matching each definition.

clue.text: Contract women tend to break

indicators.note: breaking the words apart and resetting the pieces means the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ladies usually breach agreements.
explanation.definitionFit: An endowment is a type of life insurance policy, a contract that pays out at maturity.

clue.text: Many get longer to get upset and cross

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, i.e. many

indicators.note: upsetting the letters knocks them out of order, so they are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Lots of people grow irritable as things drag on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' reads as angry; here it is a noun, a crossbreed.
explanation.definitionFit: A mongrel is a dog of mixed breed, i.e. a cross between breeds.

clue.text: It helps people to get their bearings

definitions.text: It helps people to get their bearings

parts.words: It helps people to get their bearings
parts.note: bearings here are heraldic devices on a coat of arms, and this body grants them

explanation.surface: Something like a compass or map helping lost people find their way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bearings' suggests navigation; in heraldry armorial bearings are the devices on a shield. The College of Arms is the English heraldic authority.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic definition: the official English body that grants coats of arms, i.e. armorial bearings.

clue.text: It's mostly hard work for ex-tennis champion

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: graft is informal British for hard work

explanation.surface: A former tennis star's career was largely toil.
explanation.definitionFit: Steffi Graf is a German former world number one tennis player with 22 Grand Slam titles.

clue.text: Sticking out for guide leader on organised round trip

indicators.note: organising the letters sets them in a new order
the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A tour guide sticks out ahead of a package round trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organised' rearranges ROUNDTRIP into PROTRUDIN, and G, the first letter from 'guide leader', goes at the end; 'on' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To protrude is to stick out beyond a surface; both phrases are present participles.

clue.text: Big wave producing harm in front of ship

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other, the harm going within the ship's front

parts.note: the bow is the forward end of a ship
ill means harm, as in 'wish someone ill'

explanation.surface: A huge wave crashing at a ship's bow causes damage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Front of ship' looks like a first-letter pick, S, but it gives BOW whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A billow is a great swelling wave of the sea.

clue.text: Mark's follower starts close but becomes indifferent

parts.note: in the New Testament the Gospel of Luke follows the Gospel of Mark
in guessing games you are warm when close to the answer

explanation.surface: Someone who follows Mark begins keenly but loses interest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark's follower' reads as a disciple; it is the next gospel in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Lukewarm, literally tepid, is used figuratively to mean lacking enthusiasm, indifferent.

clue.text: No cure possible — time for support

indicators.note: a possible version of the letters is one of their potential rearrangements

parts.note: an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: There's no remedy, so all that remains is moral support for a patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No cure' suggests a hopeless patient, but 'possible' is the signal to rearrange those six letters, and 'support' is the verb sense of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To encourage is to give support and confidence to someone; both verbs.

clue.text: Watchmen who stick to the rules?

definitions.meaning: people who keep or obey rules, as one keeps a law or custom

explanation.surface: Guards who follow regulations to the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Observers are both onlookers and people who keep or obey laws and customs.

clue.text: A sweet sort of baby

definitions.meaning: a wobbly gelatine dessert or a soft fruit sweet
a ... baby is a British baby-shaped gummy sweet

explanation.surface: Describing an infant as a lovely, sweet sort.
explanation.walkthrough: A jelly baby is a British gummy sweet shaped like a baby.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a gelatine sweet and, before 'baby', the British gummy sweet.

clue.text: Fur-clad Soviet leader in Russian build-up

indicators.note: being clad means being wrapped, so the fur goes round the letter

parts.note: mink is a prized fur

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A Soviet premier wrapped in fur during a Russian military build-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soviet leader' looks like Lenin or Stalin; it is just S. 'Build-up' means built-up area, a city; Minsk, now the capital of Belarus, was a Soviet city.
explanation.definitionFit: A city is a built-up area, and Minsk was a city of the Soviet, Russian-led union.

clue.text: Heinous confusion within a company

indicators.note: confusion means disorder, so the letters are muddled into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Disarray inside a firm described as wicked.
explanation.definitionFit: In-house work is carried out by a firm's own staff, internally.

clue.text: Expertise shown, taking on brother's house

indicators.note: taking something in means holding it within, so the skill encloses the small word

parts.note: mastery is expert skill

explanation.surface: Skill is displayed as a monk takes on his community.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking on' looks like a phrase; 'on' is the piece put inside MASTERY. A brother here is a monk.
explanation.definitionFit: A monastery is the home of a community of monks, or brothers.

clue.text: Opposed to profits at outset

indicators.note: read as 'set out', the two letters are set outside the other piece

parts.note: gains are profits

explanation.surface: Someone objects to making money from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outset' reads as 'the beginning' but is split as 'set out': the first piece is set outside the profits.
explanation.definitionFit: Against is a preposition meaning in opposition to.

clue.text: Storm about like a politician in a tantrum

indicators.note: the politician's letters are placed inside the tantrum

parts.note: a rage is a fit of anger
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Someone charges around like an MP throwing a fit.
explanation.walkthrough: AMP goes inside RAGE, after the R; 'like' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: To rampage is to rush about violently, i.e. to storm about.

clue.text: There's a change of name for a Biblical queen

indicators.note: a change in the letters means they are rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: The queen in the Bible was renamed.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is apt: Esther's Hebrew name was Hadassah, so she did change her name.
explanation.definitionFit: Esther is the Jewish queen of Persia in the Old Testament book named after her.

clue.text: Charm is a curious personal quality

indicators.note: curious means odd, so the letters come out in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Charm is described as a strange trait.
explanation.definitionFit: Charisma is a compelling personal charm that attracts others.

clue.text: Fall back in common mutual defence

indicators.note: back means the run is read in reverse
the letters sit inside the words common mutual

explanation.surface: Retreating to a shared defensive alliance.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside 'commoN MUTUAl' read backwards; 'defence' is surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: Fall is the American word for the season between summer and winter.

clue.text: Get thinner and lighter

definitions.meaning: to narrow gradually toward one end
a thin candle or wax spill used to light something

explanation.surface: Lose weight and become less heavy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lighter' looks like 'less heavy' but is a spill used to light a fire or lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: A taper narrows gradually, and a taper is a slender candle or spill for lighting.

clue.text: He has power over the rest of us

definitions.text: He has power over the rest of us

parts.words: He has power over the rest of us
parts.note: read as one being whose powers exceed those of ordinary mortals

explanation.surface: A tyrant who dominates everybody else.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a ruler; the sense is someone with powers beyond ordinary people.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic definition: a being whose abilities exceed those of ordinary people.

clue.text: Blueprint for a tailless aircraft

indicators.note: without its tail the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a plane is an aircraft

explanation.surface: Designs for a flying-wing aeroplane with no tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tailless aircraft' sounds like a real design; it is PLANE minus its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A blueprint is a detailed scheme or design for something.

clue.text: Many make certain you get the blame

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, i.e. many
to ensure is to make certain

explanation.surface: Lots of people make sure you are held responsible.
explanation.definitionFit: Censure is strong official criticism, i.e. blame.

clue.text: Politicians get the point first in these jokes

indicators.note: first means the compass point goes at the front, before the politicians

parts.note: S is south, a point of the compass
Tories are members of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Politicians are the first to see the punchline in these gags.
explanation.walkthrough: TORIES are members of Britain's Conservative Party; 'the point' looks like a punchline but is a compass letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Stories are tales, including funny ones told as jokes.
